chunks: By Allah, how bad are you for igniting the flames of war!
You are intrigued against but do not intrigue (against the enemy). Your boundaries are decreasing but you do not get enraged over it.
Those against you do not sleep but you are unmindful. By Allah, those who leave matters one for the other are subdued.
By Allah, I believed about you that if battle rages and death hovers around you, you will cut away from son of Abi Talib like the severing of head from the trunk.

key_terms.الْمُتَخَاذِلُونَ: Those who are negligent or leave matters to one another
key_terms.انْفِرَاجَ الرَّأْسِ: Severing of the head (metaphor for easy separation)

ai.seo_question: What criticism does Imam Ali levy against the people of Syria regarding their military and political behavior?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) addresses the people of Syria (specifically the Kufans or troops under their command) with a vivid metaphor of 'fire's rage' to describe their internal discord and strategic paralysis. He criticizes their 'ghaflah' (heedlessness) and lack of decisive action, predicting that when the battle intensifies, they will easily abandon him, fulfilling the prophecy of the 'defeated who are negligent.' This reflects the Shia scholarly view on the political and spiritual failings that led to the Battle of Siffin.
